{{Top}}
[[File:Battle_of_Geonosis.png|thumb|right|300px|A ground [[First Battle of Geonosis/Legends|battle]] between the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]] and [[Confederacy of Independent Systems/Legends|Confederacy of Independent Systems]].]]
'''Ground warfare''' related to the use of infantry and ground vehicles to engage other ground units on a [[Planet/Legends|planet's]] surface. Along with [[Space warfare/Legends|space warfare]] and [[Starfighter combat/Legends|starfighter combat]], by [[0 BBY/Legends|0 BBY]] ground warfare was one of the three most significant branches of warfighting. Ground battles and the tactics employed during them were modified throughout the [[Millennium/Legends|millennia]] spanning from the first combats between primitive civilizations to the formation of organized militias and other military forces, to the invention of the [[Blaster/Legends|blaster]] and the [[Repulsorlift/Legends|repulsorlift]], to the construction of the first [[Battle droid/Legends|battle droids]].

==Technology==
===Infantry===
{{Quote|Give me ground troops supported by airpower with supply lines guarded by the navy, and I'll promise you anything. Give me anything else and all I can do is my best.|[[General/Legends|General]] [[Alix Balan]]|<ref name="The Essential Guide to Warfare">''[[The Essential Guide to Warfare]]''</ref>}}
[[File:Clone_Troopers_Phase_II.jpg|thumb|right|250px|[[Clone trooper/Legends|Clone trooper]] infantry of the [[Grand Army of the Republic/Legends|Grand Army of the Republic]] sporting a wide variety of weapons.]]
By far the most numerous component of any [[Army/Legends|army]], [[Infantry/Legends|infantry]] were [[Soldier/Legends|soldiers]] who fought on foot to close with, assault, capture and occupy enemy positions. Throughout history, infantry had been equipped with a huge variety of weapons, which could be categorized as either ranged weapons or [[Melee weapon/Legends|melee weapons]]. By the period of the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]], the former category was almost universally represented by some kind of [[Rifle/Legends|rifle]], whether a [[Slugthrower/Legends|slugthrower]] or a [[Blaster/Legends|blaster]].<ref name="The New Essential Guide to Weapons and Technology">''[[The New Essential Guide to Weapons and Technology]]''</ref> Historical examples of ranged weapons (some of which were still used by more primitive species) included thrown [[Spear/Legends|spears]], [[Bow/Legends|bows]] and [[Arrow/Legends|arrows]], and [[lanvarok]]s. While ranged weapons technology had become fairly standardized across [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]] by [[0 BBY/Legends|0 BBY]], a large number of species continued to use their own traditional weapons or combined them with new technology: [[Wookiee/Legends|Wookiee]] [[Bowcaster/Legends|bowcasters]] and [[Chiss/Legends|Chiss]] [[Charric/Legends|charrics]] were the equals of any [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Imperial]] blaster, while despite emerging from a completely different technology base, [[Gungan/Legends|Gungan]] [[Cesta/Legends|cestas]], [[Atlatl/Legends|atlatls]], and [[Booma/Legends|boomas]] proved more than capable of disabling [[B1-series battle droid/Legends|B1-Series battle droids]] at the [[Battle of Naboo/Legends|Battle of Naboo]]. When they [[Yuuzhan Vong War|invaded]] the galaxy in [[25 ABY/Legends|25 ABY]], the [[Yuuzhan Vong]] brought with them a bizarre array of organic weapons, including [[amphistaff]]s capable of spitting venom up to twenty meters, and [[Nang hul|thud bugs]], [[razor bug]]s and [[blast bug]]s that could be hurled in great swarms at the enemy.<ref name="The New Essential Guide to Weapons and Technology">''[[The New Essential Guide to Weapons and Technology]]''</ref>

[[Melee weapon/Legends|Melee weapons]] were used when infantry had closed to close-quarters during an assault, and could include [[Knife/Legends|knives]], [[Sword/Legends|swords]], [[Polearm/Legends|polearms]] and [[Axe/Legends|axes]]. For soldiers of the [[Imperial Era/Legends|Imperial Period]], [[Vibroblade/Legends|vibroblades]] were the most common melee weapon. An uncommon but nevertheless extremely well-known melee weapon was the [[Lightsaber/Legends|lightsaber]] of the [[Jedi Knight/Legends|Jedi Knights]], which developed a reputation of being able to cut through anything and in the hands of a skilled [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]], could be used to deflect blaster bolts.<ref name="The New Essential Guide to Weapons and Technology">''[[The New Essential Guide to Weapons and Technology]]''</ref>

Infantry of the Imperial Period could additionally carry explosive [[Grenade/Legends|grenades]] to help clear enemy positions, anti-vehicle or anti-structures [[Missile launcher/Legends|missile launchers]], [[Sniper rifle/Legends|sniper rifles]] to harass the enemy at a distance, area denial weapons like [[Mine/Legends|mines]], and [[Repeating blaster/Legends|repeating blasters]] to suppress the enemy.<ref name="The New Essential Guide to Weapons and Technology">''[[The New Essential Guide to Weapons and Technology]]''</ref> The most basic infantry tactic was to fix an enemy in position with ranged weapons to allow other soldiers to close with and destroy the enemy in close quarters.

Infantry could also have varying equipment depending on the environment or situation of a ground warfare campaign. For instance, the [[Stormtrooper Corps/Legends|Stormtrooper Corps]] had various types of [[Stormtrooper/Legends|Stormtroopers]] for varying environments, from aquatic-based [[Aquatic assault stormtrooper|seatroopers]], to wetland-based [[Wetland assault stormtrooper|swamptroopers]], to Geologic-based [[Magma stormtrooper|lavatroopers]], to even [[Radiation zone assault trooper|Radtroopers]] for heavy radiation zones, with their armor and training being supplied specifically to deal with these situations.<ref name="Imperial Handbook">''[[Star Wars: Imperial Handbook: A Commander's Guide]]''</ref>

===Vehicles===
[[File:JuggernautROTS.jpg|thumb|left|250px|Wheeled vehicles, [[Walker/Legends|walkers]] and [[Repulsorcraft/Legends|repulsorcraft]] at the [[Battle of Kashyyyk/Legends|Battle of Kashyyyk]].]]
[[Assault vehicle/Legends|Assault vehicles]] were used by armies for their mobility, protection and firepower, which could be used to support, complement, and increase the mobility of infantry. Armored fighting vehicles evolved out of the use of animals in war, such as the [[Kaadu/Legends|kaadus]] of the [[Gungan Grand Army/Legends|Gungan Grand Army]] which served as rapid response shock cavalry, and the [[Sith war behemoth|war behemoths]] of the ancient [[Sith Empire/Legends|Sith Empire]], which marched into battle with massive gun turrets on their backs to smash enemy formations.<ref name="The Essential Guide to Warfare" /> Even by the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]], animals were still used when environmental conditions made vehicles unusable: the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Rebel Alliance]] made heavy use of [[Scout/Legends|scouts]] mounted on [[Tauntaun/Legends|Tauntauns]] at [[Echo Base/Legends|Echo Base]] on [[Hoth/Legends|Hoth]].<ref name="Star Wars: Episode V The Empire Strikes Back">{{Film|V}}</ref>

Vehicles could be categorized based on their form of locomotion, which included [[wheel]]s, [[Repulsorlift/Legends|repulsorlifts]], and massive [[Walker/Legends|armored legs]]. By the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]], wheeled vehicles were considered a graceless form of technology from a bygone age, but the wheeled [[HAVw A6 Juggernaut/Legends|HAVw A6 Juggernaut's]] direct ground contact protected it against electromagnetic attacks and shield discharges.<ref name="ROTS-ICS">''[[Star Wars: Revenge of the Sith Incredible Cross-Sections]]''</ref> However, the need for a low-riding chassis impeded the range of their line-of-sight weapons and reduced their terrain-handling capability. Repulsorcraft were typically faster and could handle terrain better than wheeled vehicles and walkers, and could rise above obstacles to give their guns a better aim, but their drive units were easy targets for [[Land mine/Legends|land mines]] and [[Missile/Legends|missiles]] with a [[Gravity-Activated Mode guided missile|Gravity-Activated Mode]] and they could not pass through shield perimeters. [[Walker/Legends|Walkers]] had all the advantages of a wheeled vehicle and could increase the range of their weapons by elevating them on tall [[Limb/Legends|legs]], but they were typically maintenance-heavy. Thus, an army would use a balanced mix of armored vehicles. According to the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire's]] military doctrine, heavy walkers were best used by elite assault divisions in frontal attacks on enemy fortresses, while [[Hovertank/Legends|repulsortanks]] and other such repulsorlift vehicles were better suited for "mid-intensity" combat, such as urban warfare and fast-moving campaigns in grassy or forested terrain.<ref name="The Essential Guide to Warfare" />

Vehicles could also be classified according to role. [[Tank/Legends|Tanks]] and heavy walkers like the [[All Terrain Armored Transport/Legends|All Terrain Armored Transport]] were used in frontal assaults against enemy fortifications. [[Speeder bike/Legends|Speeder bikes]] and light walkers like the [[All Terrain Scout Transport/Legends|All Terrain Scout Transport]] and [[All Terrain Recon Transport/Legends|All Terrain Recon Transport]] were used for reconnaissance, screening the flanks of an assault, and pursuing retreating enemies.<ref name="Star Wars: Complete Locations 2005">[[Star Wars: Complete Locations (2005)|''Star Wars: Complete Locations'']]</ref> Under the "flying force" doctrine of the last decades of the Galactic Republic, speeder bikes and [[Swoop/Legends|swoops]] were popular among regular light cavalry units, including the [[Single Trooper Aerial Platform/Legends|Single Trooper Aerial Platforms]] of the [[Separatist Droid Army/Legends|Separatist Droid Army]] and the [[Biker Advanced Recon Commando/Legends|Biker Advanced Recon Commandos]] of the Grand Army of the Republic. [[Troop carrier/Legends|Troop carriers]] like the [[All Terrain Tactical Enforcer/Legends|All Terrain Tactical Enforcer]], the [[All Terrain Open Transport/Legends|All Terrain Open Transport]], and the [[Multi-Troop Transport/Legends|Multi-Troop Transport]] could carry large numbers of infantry into battle under heavy protection and firepower. Militarized [[Airspeeder/Legends|airspeeders]] like the [[Low Altitude Assault Transport/Legends|Low Altitude Assault Transport]] or the [[V-wing airspeeder]] could provide extremely heavy close air support to friendly troops on the ground.<ref name="The Essential Guide to Warfare" />

Although the term "ground warfare" would generally imply constant use of hovercrafts and more terrestrial-based vehicles, it can also apply to the usage of vehicles and vessels that are more maritime-based in nature should the conflict in question occur on a more aquatic-based planet or simply if the current ground campaign was near water. The [[Imperial Maritime Division]] of the [[Imperial Army/Legends|Imperial Army]] was utilized for maritime-based battles during ground warfare which included various vehicles and equipment meant for more aquatic use.<ref name="Imperial Handbook" />

===Artillery===
[[File:SPHA-T.jpg|thumb|right|200px|Republic artillery on [[Geonosis/Legends|Geonosis]].]]
[[Artillery/Legends|Artillery]] referred to large weapons designed to fire far beyond the range and power of infantry weapons, and could be immobile, towed, or vehicle mounted. It could include anything from the [[Gungan catapult/Legends|energy catapults]] of the Gungans to the most powerful [[blaster artillery]]. Artillery included [[Mortar/Legends|mortars]] like the [[Merr-Sonn Munitions, Inc./Legends|Merr-Sonn]] [[MM-s3 grenade launcher]], which could project [[Fragmentation grenade/Legends|fragmentation grenades]] up to a kilometer, and could be mounted on a [[WW-676 repulsorlift sled]] to create a mobile fire support weapon. Anti-infantry batteries like the [[DF.9/Legends|DF.9]] could have a range of up to 16 kilometers, and could be immobile emplacement weapons or mounted on a [[Hoversled/Legends|hoversled]] to act as a mobile support gun.<ref name="The Essential Guide to Weapons and Technology">''[[The Essential Guide to Weapons and Technology]]''</ref> Anti-vehicle pieces like the [[AV-7 Antivehicle Cannon/Legends|AV-7]] had built in repulsorlifts, allowing it to be towed until it reached a suitable firing position where it would entrench itself on the ground.<ref name="Star Wars: The Clone Wars film">[[Star Wars: The Clone Wars (film)|''Star Wars: The Clone Wars'' film]]</ref> By the end of the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]], the [[New Republic/Legends|New Republic]] had replaced nearly all its fixed artillery pieces with repulsorlift-equipped units.<ref name="The New Essential Guide to Weapons and Technology">''[[The New Essential Guide to Weapons and Technology]]''</ref>

Some mobile artillery units were large enough and armored enough to be entirely self-contained vehicles, an example being the [[Self-Propelled Heavy Artillery|SPHA]] series of the [[Grand Army of the Republic/Legends|Grand Army of the Republic]], which could carry a [[Capital ship/Legends|capital ship]]-scale [[Turbolaser/Legends|turbolaser]] capable of blasting through the heaviest shielding and fortifications.<ref name="Star Wars: Episode II Attack of the Clones">{{Film|II}}</ref> Because [[Laser cannon/Legends|laser cannons]] were inherently line-of-sight weapons, the SPHA series included a number of indirect fire variants, including the [[Self-Propelled Heavy Artillery/Legends|SPHA-C]] [[Concussion missile/Legends|concussion missile]] launcher and the [[Self-Propelled Heavy Artillery/Legends|SPHA-M]] [[Mass-driver cannon/Legends|mass-driver cannon]].<ref name="The New Essential Guide to Vehicles and Vessels">''[[The New Essential Guide to Vehicles and Vessels]]''</ref> Further developments in [[blaster artillery]] resulted in the development of the [[MAS-2xB]] [[Turbolaser/Legends|turbolaser]] by the [[New Republic era]], which was used as a heavy siege weapon in the most important ground battles.<ref name="The Essential Guide to Weapons and Technology">''[[The Essential Guide to Weapons and Technology]]''</ref>

===Battle droids===
[[File:Battle_Droids_Geonosis.png|thumb|left|200px|B1 [[Battle droid/Legends|battle droids]] in action during the [[First Battle of Geonosis/Legends|Battle of Geonosis]].]]
[[Battle droid/Legends|Battle droids]] were a constant feature of ground warfare throughout history, but their effectiveness on the battlefield varied dramatically. Battle droids were attractive in that an armored droid could withstand far more punishment than an organic soldier, and could carry more weapons than an entire infantry [[Squad/Legends|squad]]. They could also be built, programmed and equipped far more quickly, easily and cheaply than recruiting and training organics. However, droids could be easily out-thought in battle and living beings often proved to be far better at improvising in the heat of battle.<ref name="The New Essential Guide to Droids">''[[The New Essential Guide to Droids]]''</ref>

War droids first appeared on the galactic stage with the [[Rakatan guardian droid]]s of the [[Infinite Empire/Legends|Infinite Empire]].<ref name="Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic">''[[Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic]]''</ref> Their most famous early use, however, was in the [[war-robot]]s of [[Xim/Legends|Xim the Despot]]. The [[Juggernaut war droid]]s of the ancient Republic was a move to the mass use of battle droids, but development was rapidly halted when they were a key component in the [[Great Droid Revolution]] of [[4015 BBY]]. The galaxy thereafter regarded battle droids with fear and revulsion, a perception only increased by the greatest use of battle droids in history during the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]]: the [[Separatist Droid Army/Legends|Separatist Droid Army]] consisted of trillions of [[B1-series battle droid/Legends|B1]], [[B2-series super battle droid/Legends|B2]], [[Droideka/Legends|droideka]], [[IG-227 Hailfire-class droid tank/Legends|Hailfire]] and [[OG-9 homing spider droid/Legends|spider]] battle droids. This was the apex of battle droid use, and thereafter, the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]], [[New Republic/Legends|New Republic]] and [[Galactic Federation of Free Alliances|Galactic Alliance]] would only sporadically resort to the use of battle droids, and then only in very small numbers. Famous post-Clone Wars examples of battle droids like the [[Dark Trooper/Legends|Dark Troopers]] and the [[YVH-Series battle droid|YVH-Series]] were exceptions that proved a rather ironclad rule.<ref name="The Essential Guide to Warfare" />

===Combat support===
{{Quote|COMETS-Q! Yessir, it's COMETS-Q that gets you to the battlefield, sustains you once you're there, and gets you home again!|[[Quartermaster/Legends|Quartermaster]] [[Mess Boulanger]]|<ref name="Jedi Trial">''[[Jedi Trial]]''</ref>}}
Just as important as weapons and vehicles, and without which they could not function, was combat support, including logistics, engineering, communications, and medics. During the Clone Wars, [[Quartermaster/Legends|quartermasters]] and [[Logistics officer/Legends|logistics officers]] used the acronym [[COMETS-Q]] to refer to the seven elements of combat support: Chemical, Ordnance, Medical, Engineer, Transportation, Signal and Quartermaster.<ref name="Jedi Trial" />

''Chemical'' referred to protection measures taken against [[:Category: Chemical weaponry|chemical weapons]] like [[Fex-M3/Legends|Fex-M3]] or [[Dioxis/Legends|dioxis]]. The clone troopers of the Republic and their successors, the Imperial [[Stormtrooper/Legends|Stormtroopers]], wore full suits of [[Stormtrooper armor/Legends|sealed white armor]] to filter out chemical, radiological and biological contaminants.<ref name="The New Essential Guide to Weapons and Technology">''[[The New Essential Guide to Weapons and Technology]]''</ref> Other militaries issued [[Breath mask/Legends|breath masks]] for the purpose.<ref name="The Essential Guide to Weapons and Technology">''[[The Essential Guide to Weapons and Technology]]''</ref> Other measures against chemical weapons might include field decontamination centers for affected personnel.<ref name="Star Wars: Attack of the Clones Incredible Cross-Sections">''[[Star Wars: Attack of the Clones Incredible Cross-Sections]]''</ref>

''Ordnance'' referred to the procurement, storage and maintenance of large amounts of ammunition, which could be as diverse as [[Bomb/Legends|bombs]], [[Missile/Legends|missiles]], [[Blaster gas/Legends|blaster gas]], [[Blaster power pack/Legends|blaster power packs]], and grenades.<ref name="The Rebel Alliance Sourcebook">''[[The Rebel Alliance Sourcebook]]''</ref> ''Medical'' referred to procedures for preventing and treating injuries and maladies. It was a truism that throughout military history, disease had killed more soldiers than actual combat. By the Clone Wars this was no longer true, with [[Medical droid/Legends|medical droids]] like the [[IM-6 Battlefield Medical Droid/Legends|IM-6]] stabilizing injured soldiers in the field, before they were triaged and transferred by [[Medlifter troop transport|medlifter]] to field [[Medcenter/Legends|medcenters]] like the [[Republic Mobile Surgical Unit/Legends|Republic Mobile Surgical Units]] for treatment with [[Bacta/Legends|bacta]], [[Organ replacement/Legends|cloned organ replacement]], or [[Cybernetics/Legends|cybernetic replacement limbs]].<ref name="Star Wars: The Essential Guide to Warfare Author's Cut">{{SW|url=news/the-essential-guide-to-warfare-authors-cut-part-7-the-grand-army-of-the-republic|series=Star Wars: The Essential Guide to Warfare Author's Cut|text=Part 7 &mdash; The Grand Army of the Republic}}</ref>

''Engineer'' referred to repair, construction and demolition activities made under field conditions.<ref name="Star Wars: Battlefront">''[[Star Wars: Battlefront]]''</ref> ''Transportation'' referred to the shipping of troops and materiel to support the engagement, which could be a complex task that might not always meet the supply demands of troops at the front: at the [[Battle of Praesitlyn]] during the Clone Wars, the Republic army consumed 2000 metric tons of supplies per day of operation while resupply could only occur at a rate of 1000 tons per day, and with a high number of transport casualties. ''Signal'' referred to military communications made through technology such as [[Comlink/Legends|comlinks]], as well as countermeasures such as [[Jammer/Legends|jammers]]. Finally, ''Quartermaster'' referred to those military personnel responsible for supply and support.<ref name="Jedi Trial" />

==History==
===Ancient wars===
{{Quote|They polished their fearsome helms, that they might flash even in the weak sun of Notron. They rewrapped the hilts of their weapons and pounded straight the shafts, that they might slake their thirst in Zhell ichor a final time.|''[[Dha Werda Verda]]''|<ref name="The Essential Guide to Warfare" />}}
[[File:Hutt_Xim_war.jpg|thumb|right|300px|The [[Third Battle of Vontor]].]]
The first ground battles took place between [[Army/Legends|armies]] equipped with [[Spear/Legends|spears]] and [[Sword/Legends|swords]], for example, the [[Taung/Legends|Taungs]] and the [[Battalions of Zhell]] in their [[Zhell–Taung war|ancient war]] on [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]]. Subsequent developments included [[Slugthrower/Legends|slugthrowers]] and [[wheel]]ed armored vehicles. Technology developing at different paces could create armies using eclectic mixes of equipment: [[Rakata/Legends|Rakatan]] infantry of the [[Infinite Empire/Legends|Infinite Empire]] were known to go into battle with swords and shocklances while being supported by [[Rakatan guardian droid|ancient battle droids]] equipped with [[Blaster/Legends|blasters]] and primitive [[Starfighter/Legends|starfighters]].<ref name="The Essential Guide to Warfare" /><ref name="Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic">''[[Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic]]''</ref>

An extremely well-documented ancient military was that of [[Xim's empire]]. [[Xim/Legends|Xim the Despot's]] military was extremely advanced for its day, built from lost [[Rakata/Legends|Rakatan]] technology. The scale of his armies and conquests meant that numerous examples of Xim's weaponry survived to the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]] era. Xim's [[Infantry/Legends|infantry]] were divided into several castes. Most were [[Janissary/Legends|janissaries]] taken from occupied worlds, trained from childhood to serve as soldiers. They wore [[Armor/Legends|armor]] and helmets of lightweight ceramic alloy and carried either [[Slugthrower/Legends|slugthrowers]] or [[heatbeam]]s, which used [[Laser/Legends|lasers]] to generate jets of [[Plasma/Legends|plasma]]. Heatbeamers wore tough, fireproof padded gloves and [[Kama/Legends|''kamas'']] a protection against their weapons' superheated exhausts. The ''kama'' would later be adopted by the [[Thyrsus/Legends|Thyrsus]] [[Sun Guard]] and by the [[Mandalorian/Legends|Mandalorian]] people as part of their culture. Among Xim's elite units were the [[Duinarbulon Star Lancers]], who wore gloss-black ceramic armor and in addition to traditional [[Spear/Legends|lances]], carried advanced [[Beam tube/Legends|beam tubes]], distant ancestors of the [[Blaster/Legends|blaster]]. The infantry was supported by tracked tanks, armored [[Groundcar/Legends|groundcars]], and [[floater]]s armed with beam tube cannons. Elite vehicles were armored with [[Kiirium/Legends|kiirium]] to reflect energy weapons. Xim's most famous soldiers were the war-robots of the [[Guardian Corps]], three-meter tall [[Battle droid/Legends|battle droids]] armed with heatbeams, particle dischargers, and [[pulse-wave cannon]]s. The War-Robots were typically kept in reserve for use as shock troops.<ref name="The Essential Guide to Warfare" />

Xim's forces were ultimately defeated in his [[Xim Wars|final war]] with the [[Hutt Empire]]. Little is known about ancient Hutt warriors, but ancient [[Sakiyan/Legends|Sakiyan]] chronicles recorded Hutt cavaliers armored with iron shells and maneuvering via metal limbs, treads or wheels. These would later be compared to the [[Shell Hutts]] of [[Circumtore/Legends|Circumtore]].<ref name="The Essential Guide to Warfare" /> At the [[Third Battle of Vontor]], Xim's war-robots and other infantry were overwhelmed by vast numbers of [[Spice/Legends|spice]]-maddened [[Nikto/Legends|Nikto]], [[Vodran/Legends|Vodran]] and [[Klatooinian/Legends|Klatooinian]] warriors, spelling an end to the Despot's dominion.<ref name="Xim Week">{{SW|url=news/essential-atlas-extra-the-history-of-xim-and-the-tion-cluster|text=Essential Atlas Extra: The History of Xim and the Tion Cluster|int=Xim Week: The History of Xim and the Tion Cluster}}</ref>

===The Wars of the Republic===
[[File:Battle_of_Coruscant_Great_Hyperspace_War.jpg|thumb|right|250px|The [[Great Hyperspace War/Legends|Great Hyperspace War]] was fought with both ancient and modern technology.]]
The early [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]] was founded without an [[Republic Army|army]] or [[Republic Navy/Legends|navy]], but the [[Tionese War]] of [[24,000 BBY|24,000]]-[[23,900 BBY]] forced it to become a centralized military power.<ref name="The Essential Guide to Warfare" /> Throughout its long history, the [[Republic Army]] and the [[Planetary Security Forces]] would fight many ground battles.

Ground warfare was a perennial feature of the [[Pius Dea Crusades]] from c. [[12,000 BBY/Legends|12,000]] to c. [[11,000 BBY]]. [[Pius Dea]] [[cathedral ship]]s would deploy troops by the millions onto planets that were deemed impure by the religious cult and were to be occupied, plundered and purified. Attritional trench warfare was a feature of these many battles.<ref name="The Essential Guide to Warfare" />

During the [[Waymancy Storm]] of [[7811 BBY]], the [[Republic Military/Legends|Republic Military]] found its best [[Beam tube/Legends|beam tubes]], [[heatbeam]]s and [[plasma caster]]s entirely outclassed by the [[pulse-wave blaster]]s of [[Waymancy Hollow]], which used the [[Sif-Alulan process]] to create much more powerful, faster firing weapons. Millions died both in space and on the ground before the Republic successfully reverse-engineered Waymancy weapons to create the [[squintpipe process]] and its own pulse-wave blasters. [[Rocket-Jumper Elite Advance Unit|Republic Rocket-Jumpers]] armed with pulse-wave carbines won one of the Republic's first victories in the conflict by routing the [[Neshtab]]ine nest in the [[Tantara system/Legends|Tantara system]].<ref name="Author's Cut 4">{{SW|url=news/the-essential-guide-to-warfare-authors-cut-part-4-the-rise-of-the-republic-needs-author-entry|series=Star Wars: The Essential Guide to Warfare Author's Cut|text=Part 4: The Rise of the Republic}}</ref> By the 7500s BBY, further advances in the squintpipe process had produced strong, reliable, and portable [[Deflector shield/Legends|deflector shields]], allowing armies to make use of large [[Planetary shield/Legends|planetary shields]] to protect fortifications. However, ground vehicles were rarely equipped with shields, and [[Personal energy shield/Legends|personal energy shields]] faded from military use after the [[Jedi Civil War]]: personal shields required large power packs that needed frequent replacement, exposed their users to unhealthy magnetic and radioactive forces, and could fail catastrophically with fatal results.<ref name="The Essential Guide to Warfare" />

[[Blaster/Legends|Blaster]] technology continued to mature from [[7000 BBY]], however problems related to pulse-wave weapons' accuracy and range meant that [[Melee weapon/Legends|melee weapons]] were still a decisive component of armies' arsenals, particularly the [[Lightsaber/Legends|lightsabers]] of the [[Jedi Knight/Legends|Jedi Knights]]. This was seen most clearly during the [[Great Hyperspace War/Legends|Great Hyperspace War]] of [[5000 BBY/Legends|5000 BBY]], when forces of the [[Sith Empire/Legends|Sith Empire]] led by [[Naga Sadow/Legends|Naga Sadow]] [[Battle of Coruscant (Great Hyperspace War)|invaded Coruscant]]. Sith [[Massassi/Legends|Massassi]] warriors fought with [[pulse-wave rifle]]s alongside their traditional [[Polearm/Legends|baradiches]] and [[Massassi lanvarok|lanvarok throwing discs]], and [[Cannon/Legends|cannon]] [[Turret/Legends|turrets]] crowned the backs of elephantine [[Sith war behemoth|war behemoths]]. Throwing discs could skim through [[Deflector shield/Legends|deflector shields]], and war beasts could stride where armored vehicles could not. The Republic opposed them with [[blaster artillery]] supporting armies of [[Spear/Legends|spear]]-wielding [[Infantry/Legends|infantry]], led by lightsaber-armed Jedi.<ref name="The Essential Guide to Warfare" />

[[File:BattleOfAlderaan-TORHope.png|thumb|left|250px|Republic troops, more heavily armed and armored than their [[Old Sith Wars]] counterparts, engage the [[Imperial Army (Sith Empire)|Sith Imperial Army]] during the [[Battle of Alderaan]].]]

The blaster had matured by [[4000 BBY/Legends|4000 BBY]] and the end of the [[Great Sith War/Legends|Great Sith War]].<ref name="The Essential Guide to Warfare" /> By the start of the [[Mandalorian Wars]], the [[Republic Army]] would be recognizable to a warrior of the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]], with a familiar [[Republic Army#Tactical organization|tactical organization]], and with uniformly-equipped [[Armor/Legends|armored]] infantry armed with lightweight [[Blaster rifle/Legends|blaster rifles]].<ref name="Knights of the Old Republic Campaign Guide">''[[Knights of the Old Republic Campaign Guide]]''</ref> Similarly-equipped [[Republic soldier|soldiers]] and [[Republic trooper|troopers]] served the Republic during the [[Great Galactic War]], the [[Cold War (Galactic Republic–Sith Empire)|Cold War]], and the [[Galactic War]], fighting against the [[Imperial soldier]]s of the [[Sith Empire (Post–Great Hyperspace War)|Sith Empire]]. The [[Imperial Navy (Sith Empire)|Sith Imperial Army]] was also notable for its heavy use of [[Sith war droid|war droids]].<ref name="Star Wars: The Old Republic">''[[Star Wars: The Old Republic]]''</ref>

[[File:Battleofruusan.jpg|thumb|right|250px|The [[Seventh Battle of Ruusan]], where casualties and supply problems reduced the [[Army of Light/Legends|Army of Light]] to spears and swords in their final battle.]]

Ground warfare was a feature of the [[New Sith Wars]] from [[2000 BBY/Legends|2000]] to [[1000 BBY/Legends|1000 BBY]]. The Republic Army suffered one of the worst defeats in its history in [[1466 BBY]] when the [[New Sith]] crushed Republic and [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] forces in the [[Battle of Mizra]]. This bloody conflict was later immortalized by the poet [[Felloux]].<ref name="The New Essential Chronology">''[[The New Essential Chronology]]''</ref> Over five hundred thousand soldiers died in the battle and hundreds of Jedi converted to the Dark Side.<ref name="The Essential Atlas">''[[The Essential Atlas]]''</ref>

Around 1010 BBY, during the last years of the [[New Sith Wars]], the Republic Army was incorporated into the [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]]-led [[Army of Light/Legends|Army of Light]] under the command of [[Jedi Lord|Lord]] [[Hoth (Jedi Lord)|Hoth]]. In a grueling series of [[Ruusan campaign|Seven Battles]] on the planet [[Ruusan/Legends|Ruusan]], the Army of Light slowly ground down the Sith [[Brotherhood of Darkness/Legends|Brotherhood of Darkness]]. By the [[Seventh Battle of Ruusan]], what had begun as an advanced, combined arms army composed of [[Starfighter/Legends|starfighters]], [[Speeder bike/Legends|speeder bike]]-mounted infantry, and armored vehicle units had been reduced to a ragtag collection of local levies armed with whatever weapon was available, lending the Army of Light the appearance of a spear-wielding feudal army more appropriate to five thousand years earlier. The Army of Light eventually won a costly victory at the Seventh Battle of Ruusan, when most of the Sith were destroyed by the machinations of one of their own, [[Darth Bane/Legends|Darth Bane]].<ref name="The Essential Guide to Warfare" />

===The Rise of the Empire===
[[File:BattleOfGrassyPlains-EGTW.jpg|thumb|left|250px|B1 battle droids engage the Gungan Grand Army at the Battle of Naboo.]]
The [[Ruusan Reformations/Legends|Ruusan Reformations]] of [[1000 BBY/Legends|1000 BBY]] abolished the Republic's standing armed forces. Nevertheless, ground warfare was an unchanging feature of the Republic's final millennium, conducted by the ground troops of the [[Judicial Forces/Legends|Judicial Forces]] and the [[Planetary Security Forces]]. In the absence of a centralized military force, the galaxy's greatest megacorporations like the [[Trade Federation/Legends|Trade Federation]], the [[InterGalactic Banking Clan/Legends|InterGalactic Banking Clan]], the [[Techno Union/Legends|Techno Union]] and the [[Corporate Alliance/Legends|Corporate Alliance]] began establishing their own armies to protect their commercial operations, typically composed of large numbers of [[Battle droid/Legends|battle droids]]. As relations between the central government on Coruscant and the megacorps slowly collapsed from the [[40 BBY/Legends|40s BBY]] through to the start of the [[Separatist Crisis/Legends|Separatist Crisis]], these companies began to pursue a massive military buildup, with manufacturers like [[Baktoid Combat Automata/Legends|Baktoid Combat Automata]] and the [[Colicoid Creation Nest/Legends|Colicoid Creation Nest]] developing a number of battle droid models designed to wage war against the Republic.<ref name="The Essential Guide to Warfare" />

The [[Battle of Naboo/Legends|Battle of Naboo]] of [[32 BBY/Legends|32 BBY]] was the first deployment of large numbers of battle droids by the [[Trade Federation Droid Army/Legends|Trade Federation Droid Army]]. In a diversionary action fought on the [[Great Grass Plains/Legends|Great Grass Plains]], this force engaged with the [[Gungan Grand Army/Legends|Gungan Grand Army]] while [[Naboo (people)/Legends|Naboo]] strike teams led by [[Padmé Amidala/Legends|Padmé Amidala]] infiltrated into occupied [[Theed/Legends|Theed]] to capture [[Viceroy/Legends|Viceroy]] [[Nute Gunray/Legends|Nute Gunray]]. The battle on the plains was of a sort rarely found in galactic society: the Gungans' [[Fambaa/Legends|fambaa]] [[Deflector shield generator/Legends|shield generators]] reduced the effectiveness of the Trade Federation's [[Armored Assault Tank/Legends|Armored Assault Tanks]], and [[B1-series battle droid/Legends|B1-Series battle droid]] infantry had to be deployed to march through the shield. Consequently, the battle was fought at close range like a traditional land battle between armies largely composed of infantry, and military historians marvelled at the rare opportunity to study such an engagement.<ref name="The Essential Guide to Warfare" /><ref name="Star Wars: Episode I The Phantom Menace">{{Film|I}}</ref>

[[File:ClonetrooperFormation-AotC.jpg|thumb|right|200px|A [[Legion/Legends|legion]] of [[Clone trooper/Legends|clone troopers]] marching in formation.]]

In the aftermath of the [[Invasion of Naboo/Legends|Invasion of Naboo]], [[Jedi Master/Legends|Jedi Master]] [[Sifo-Dyas/Legends|Sifo-Dyas]] sensed that the Republic would soon face an existential threat, and approached the [[Cloning/Legends|cloners]] of [[Kamino/Legends|Kamino]] to produce a clone army for the Republic. A massive mechanized force of [[Clone trooper/Legends|clone troopers]] produced from the [[Mandalorian/Legends|Mandalorian]] [[Bounty hunter/Legends|bounty hunter]] [[Jango Fett/Legends|Jango Fett]], the [[Grand Army of the Republic/Legends|Grand Army of the Republic]] was developed in complete secrecy over ten years.<ref name="Star Wars: Episode II Attack of the Clones">{{Film|II}}</ref> Its doctrine and vehicles, ranging from [[Low Altitude Assault Transport/infantry/Legends|gunships]] and [[All Terrain Tactical Enforcer/Legends|walkers]] to [[Acclamator-class transgalactic military assault ship/Legends|assault ships]] and [[Self-Propelled Heavy Artillery|artillery]], were built around unleashing the maximum amount of force incredibly quickly. This differed from the approach seen in ground warfare for thousands of years, where armies had deployed their strength cautiously over long periods.<ref name="Star Wars: The Complete Visual Dictionary">''[[Star Wars: The Complete Visual Dictionary]]''</ref> The clone troopers were clad in [[Clone trooper armor/Legends|white full-body armor]] which protected them against heat, poison gas, impacts, and glancing hits, and were inculcated with Mandalorian warrior traditions by Fett, which proved ideal for reinforcing their genetically engineered inclination toward loyalty and unit cohesion. The Grand Army took the ancient Mandalorian marching chant ''[[Vode An]]'' ("Brothers All") as its anthem, and took as its motto ''Darasuum Kote'', "Eternal Glory" in [[Mando'a/Legends|Mando'a]].<ref name="The Essential Guide to Warfare" />

The [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]], beginning with the [[First Battle of Geonosis/Legends|First Battle of Geonosis]], were fought by the Grand Army of the Republic and the [[Separatist Droid Army/Legends|Separatist Droid Army]] across hundreds of different fronts on thousands of worlds. Generally, the Grand Army served as a rapid reaction force while the Republic's disparate [[Planetary Security Forces]] operated in defensive deployments - a number of battles in the Clone Wars were fought entirely by Planetary Security Forces without a clone trooper or a battle droid in sight. The GAR's largest operational units were the [[Sector Army/Legends|sector armies]], which typically maintained one [[Corps/Legends|corps]] intact as a rapid reaction force while splitting its other three corps into hundreds of small, fast-moving raiding companies.<ref name="The Essential Guide to Warfare" /> Known as the "[[Militia/Legends|militia]] model", this allowed small numbers of clone troopers to mobilize far larger numbers of local guerrillas and execute planetary coups, a strategy that was successful at the [[Battle of Malastare/Legends|Battle of Malastare]], the [[Battle of Haruun Kal/Legends|Battle of Haruun Kal]], and the [[Battle of Giju (Clone Wars)|Battle of Giju]].<ref name="The Essential Atlas" />

The Separatist Droid Army, meanwhile, was a hodgepodge of vast numbers of different types of battle droids, reflecting the eclectic nature of the factions that made up the CIS. In the initial months of the war, this diverse army worked together poorly, but the Republic was unable to take advantage of the Confederacy's disarray as it faced the same challenge of trying to build up its centralized army while coordinating the efforts of local forces. The Separatists pursued a defensive strategy for the first few months of the war, seeking to blunt Republic drives into their dispersed territories. Its first offensive moves were combinations of surgical strikes and terror operations, a [[stateless strategy]] designed to deny the Republic key invasion corridors, undermine support for the war, and sever key fleets' supply lines. Only after a massive military buildup and the appointment of [[General/Legends|General]] [[Grievous/Legends|Grievous]] as [[Supreme Commander of the Droid Armies/Legends|Supreme Commander of the Droid Armies]] was the CIS able to launch a sustained strike - [[Operation Durge's Lance]] - deep into Republic space. By that point of the Clone Wars, however, the Republic had been able to devote its superior industrial capacity to the war. Amid horrific attritional fighting on planets like [[Mygeeto/Legends|Mygeeto]], [[Saleucami/Legends|Saleucami]], [[Felucia/Legends|Felucia]] and [[Boz Pity/Legends|Boz Pity]] in the [[Outer Rim Sieges/Legends|Outer Rim Sieges]], the Confederacy was slowly ground down by the Grand Army of the Republic before the [[Mission to Mustafar/Legends|deactivation of the Droid Armies]] by [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Darth Vader]].<ref name="The Essential Guide to Warfare" />

===The Galactic Civil War===
[[File:ATATattack-EGTW.jpg|thumb|left|200px|AT-ATs of the [[Imperial Army/Legends|Imperial Army]] in the attack during the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]].]]
With the [[Declaration of a New Order]], the Republic was reorganized into the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]]. The clone troopers of the Grand Army became the core of the [[Stormtrooper Corps/Legends|Stormtrooper Corps]], elite shock troops whose loyalty was solely to [[Galactic Emperor/Legends|Emperor]] [[Palpatine/Legends|Palpatine]]. Meanwhile, the [[Planetary Security Forces]] were [[Imperialization/Legends|nationalized]] and they and the non-clone [[Human/Legends|humans]] of the GAR and the [[Judicial Forces/Legends|Judicials]] were transformed into the [[Imperial Army/Legends|Imperial Army]]. The human elements of the GAR were specifically placed into the Imperial Army as a means to bring Separatist sympathizers in line, owing to their experience during the Clone Wars, as well as prime itself for surface superiority.<ref name="Imperial Handbook" /> [[Imperial Army trooper/Legends|Imperial Army troopers]] garrisoned planets and piloted most of the Empire's ground assault vehicles, including [[Hovertank/Legends|repulsortanks]], [[juggernaut]]s, [[HAVr A9 Floating Fortress/Legends|floating fortresses]], and most famously, [[Walker/Legends|walkers]].> The towering [[All Terrain Armored Transport/Legends|All Terrain Armored Transport]] had first seen service at the [[Battle of Jabiim]] during the Clone Wars, and it and its lighter counterparts like the [[All Terrain Scout Transport/Legends|All Terrain Scout Transport]] and the [[All Terrain Recon Transport/Legends|All Terrain Recon Transport]] dominated the battlefield under Imperial Army doctrine. Designed for frontal assaults against enemy fortresses, these walkers were often thought to resemble ancient pachyderm cavalry, as if they had been designed in imitation of the [[Sith war behemoth|war behemoths]] of the [[Sith Empire/Legends|Sith Empire]].<ref name="The Essential Guide to Warfare" />

For all their material advantages, however, Imperial Army commanders during the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]] were noted to be somewhat uncreative, using outdated "by the book" tactics learned in the [[Imperial Academy/Legends|Imperial Academy]]. Most Imperial commanders could be more easily defeated if faced with an unexpected situation for which there was no conventional solution.<ref name="The Rebel Alliance Sourcebook">''[[The Rebel Alliance Sourcebook]]''</ref> The Imperial Army's orders generally came from a top-down aspect, whereby the Emperor supplied the orders which were transmitted from [[Army Command]] down through a clear hierarchy. In addition, Imperial commanders were expected to follow established protocol, and often did so by set objectives that defined in the type of units deployed into battle and how these units were to be used. As such, while the Imperial forces could afford to field specialized troopers in great numbers and in various formations, their Rebel counterparts in those fields tended to have greater training than Imperial specialists.<ref name="Imperial Handbook" /> The Imperial Army had a tendency to ignore complaints from civilians due to answering to the Emperor and not to citizenry, although [[Imperial Army Special Missions trooper/Legends|Imperial Army Special Missions trooper]] units generally ignored that aspect of protocol. The Imperial Army also had a tendency to treat assets with extreme callousness, such as exploiting their loyalty to the Emperor to be used in no-win combat situations. A particularly notorious example of this was [[General/Legends|General]] [[Rom Mohc]]'s treatment of the [[Ailon Nova Guard/Legends|Ailon Nova Guard]].<ref name="Imperial Handbook" />

[[File:ScoutBattle-TSS.jpg|thumb|right|250px|Imperial forces entrenched in a heavy firefight.]]
The Imperial Army's opposition in the ground warfare of the Galactic Civil War was the far smaller [[Alliance Army/Legends|Alliance Army]], whose numbers amounted to just 3.5 percent of the [[New Order/Legends|New Order's]] total military forces. In addition, the Rebel forces on most Imperial-occupied worlds could not afford open combat against Imperials because they lacked the troop strength to do so at the regimental level, while the Imperial Army could.<ref name="Imperial Handbook" /> However, this was the equivalent to Imperial occupation forces for fifteen [[Sector/Legends|sectors]], and the Alliance Army was devoted almost entirely to offensive operations. Furthermore, since the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Rebel Alliance]] was for the most part a clandestine insurgency, its strength was more impressive than a direct comparison suggested. Nevertheless, the [[Rebel trooper/Legends|Rebel troopers]] of the Alliance Army were a ragtag bunch. Organized into thousands of [[Sector Force/Legends|Sector Forces]], they had no common uniform, and differed in every way from how they might organize their units to what equipment was available. Some Sector Forces, like the [[Airam Clans]] or the [[Karthakk resistance]], could muster tens of thousands of troops with ground vehicles and artillery. Others had just a few thousand irregulars, saboteurs and agitators with only a few crates of blasters and [[Thermal detonator/Legends|thermal detonators]].<ref name="The Essential Guide to Warfare" />

The most capable Rebel soldiers were the [[Alliance Special Forces/Legends|Alliance Special Forces]], or SpecForce. Optimized for [[Commando/Legends|commando]] warfare and numbering barely one hundred thousand beings, the SpecForces were a flexible backbone for the entire Rebellion. Permanent SpecForce detachments guarded the most significant [[Rebel base]]s and barracks [[Regiment/Legends|regiments]] acted as specialist support echelons for other elements of the [[Alliance Military/Legends|Alliance Military]]. Most actual fighting was done by temporary [[Task force/Legends|task forces]] assembled on an ''ad hoc'' basis for missions, or to bolster weak Sector Forces.<ref name="The Essential Guide to Warfare" />

The Alliance's initial war plan, [[Operation Domino]], called for the strongest Sector Forces to defeat local Imperial Army garrisons in set-piece battles and then dig in behind [[Planetary shield/Legends|planetary shields]], proving that planets could free themselves from the Empire and so inspire a revolution across the galaxy. In the event, Operation Domino was a disaster, and the uprisings were rapidly crushed. Thereafter, the Alliance never tried to take and hold territory until after the [[Battle of Endor/Legends|Battle of Endor]], instead relying on the SpecForces and the [[Alliance Starfighter Corps/Legends|Starfighter Corps]] to strike at the Empire as insurgents.<ref name="The Essential Guide to Warfare" /> But for when they had to defend against set-piece Imperial attacks on their bases, such as at the [[Battle of Hoth/Legends|Battle of Hoth]], Rebel ground warfare consisted overwhelmingly of raids lasting less than a day. Conducting themselves according to General [[Crix Madine/Legends|Crix Madine's]] [[Madine's Rules of War|Rules of War]], the Rebel Alliance sought to preserve its limited military resources by using speed and maneuver, psychological warfare and unpredictability, and creatively unorthodox tactics to defeat an Imperial Military overly dependent on superior numbers and doctrinaire thinking.<ref name="The Rebel Alliance Sourcebook">''[[The Rebel Alliance Sourcebook]]''</ref>

[[File:RebelVictoryAtCoruscant.jpg|thumb|left|200px|The [[New Republic Army]] captures [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]].]]
The [[Battle of Tiems]] was a textbook example of Madine's Rules of War: making use of a mobile defense and fighting with three regiments against four Imperial, General [[Carlist Rieekan/Legends|Carlist Rieekan]] successfully drew half the Imperial force into a trap, encircling and destroying them. Though the Imperial commander had another four regiments in reserve, he waited another twelve hours for the weather to clear so his next offensive could be launched with air support, by which time Rieekan had achieved his objective and evacuated his three regiments from [[Tiems (planet)|Tiems]].<ref name="The Rebel Alliance Sourcebook">''[[The Rebel Alliance Sourcebook]]''</ref> Elsewhere in the galaxy, the Empire was repeatedly defeated by local forces with superior morale: the [[Dressellian resistance]] drove the Empire from [[Dressel/Legends|Dressel]] by making heavy use of [[Dressellian Projectile Rifle|primitive projectile rifles]], which eventually caused the Empire such high casualties that they chose to abandon the planet.<ref name="The Essential Guide to Weapons and Technology">''[[The Essential Guide to Weapons and Technology]]''</ref> At the [[Battle of Endor/Legends|Battle of Endor]], the Imperial [[Tempest Force/Legends|Tempest Force]] was overcome by [[Ewok/Legends|Ewoks]] who, despite possessing only primitive weapons, defeat them through superior natural camouflage and terrain knowledge, giving a SpecOps [[Endor strike team/Legends|strike team]] led by General [[Han Solo/Legends|Han Solo]] time to destroy the [[Endor shield generator bunker|shield generator]] protecting the orbiting [[Death Star II/Legends|Second Death Star]], winning the greatest Alliance victory in the Galactic Civil War.<ref name="Star Wars: Episode VI Return of the Jedi">{{Film|VI}}</ref>

With Emperor Palpatine's death at [[Endor/Legends|Endor]], the Alliance Army was reorganized into the [[New Republic Army]]: the SpecForces were reorganized as bridgehead commandos for planetary assault, while the rest of the Army, composed of the [[Planetary Security Forces]] the New Republic had proclaimed denationalized with the [[Defense Declarations]], served as an occupation and peacekeeping force. The Imperial Army and Stormtrooper Corps, meanwhile, suffered badly in the aftermath of Endor, split between ambitious [[Warlord/Legends|warlords]] and severely reducing the Empire's ability to resist the advance of the [[New Republic/Legends|New Republic]]. Significant post-Endor ground battles included the three-month [[Milagro campaign]], an attritional slog marked by open combat between Republic repulsortanks and Imperial AT-ATs, as well as subterranean struggles between both sides' sappers, miners, and [[Engineer/Legends|engineers]]; the savage [[Battle of Mindor]] against [[Cronal|Lord Shadowspawn]]; and the [[Liberation of Coruscant (Galactic Civil War)|Liberation of Coruscant]]. The New Republic Army suffered heavy casualties in [[Operation Shadow Hand]], however, and in the [[12 ABY/Legends|12 ABY]] reorganization of the [[New Republic Defense Force/Legends|New Republic Defense Force]], was abolished. Many of its responsibilities were transferred to the local defense forces, while the [[New Republic Marine]]s took over the planetary assault role under the command of the [[New Republic Defense Fleet/Legends|naval]] [[Battle group/Legends|battle groups]] as part of a fully-integrated Defense Force.<ref name="The Essential Guide to Warfare" />

==Strategy and tactics==
{{Quote|There are three ways to defeat your enemy. The first, and most obvious, is to better him in a trial of force. The best way is to have him destroy himself; few enemies are so obliging. The middle way is to destroy your enemy from within. Judicious application of the middle way shall make your blows more effective if you later take the way of force. From the middle way it is also possible to push your enemy onto the path of self-destruction.|[[Sayings|''The Sayings'']] of [[Uueg Tching]]|<ref name="Imperial Sourcebook">''[[Imperial Sourcebook]]''</ref>}}
Battles on the surface of a planet were conducted by an attacker to seize control of objectives, which could be as small as a single military base to as large as a [[City/Legends|city]] or even the entire planet itself. For the attacker, ground warfare comprised the invasion and control phases of a [[Planetary assault tactics|planetary assault operation]], and was possessed of numerous advantages, including the ability to supply [[Orbital bombardment/Legends|bombardments]] or [[Starfighter/Legends|starfighter]] [[Bomber/Legends|bombers]] from an orbiting fleet.<ref name="A World to Conquer">{{JournalCite|2|A World to Conquer}}</ref> The defender also had a number of advantages, however, such as the ability to dig in in entrenched positions or occupy fortresses. As seen in the [[Battle of Tiems]], an invading force might act defensively while a defending force might also act aggressively.<ref name="The Rebel Alliance Sourcebook">''[[The Rebel Alliance Sourcebook]]''</ref>

The [[Imperial Army/Legends|Imperial Army]] of the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]] identified several objectives a ground force might seek to achieve in surface missions include utterly obliterating an enemy possession; engaging enemy infantry and mechanized units; providing strategic insertion of [[Commando/Legends|commandos]] or expeditionary forces; securing control of a key planetary resource or supply line; and holding to a position and destroying enemy attackers attempting to reclaim it. These strategies emphasized demoralizing the enemy, specifically through the use of overwhelming firepower to leave them shell-shocked and helpless in the face of a massive, numerically-superior frontal assault. The Empire also emphasized striking to disrupt the enemy's plans and expose their flaws while they were in disorder. Because of the Rebels' adoption of an insurgent strategy, the Imperial Army saw its first priority as being to eradicate the existence of Rebel cells immediately and decisively, comparing the process to sterilizing a wound with heat.<ref name="Imperial Handbook" /> The Imperial Army emphasized the frontal assault as the centerpiece of ground warfare, which drove the development of massive [[Walker/Legends|walkers]] like the [[All Terrain Armored Transport/Legends|AT-AT]], which could use its immense height to deliver overwhelming firepower against targets from far outside the range of most artillery or ground vehicles.<ref name="The Essential Guide to Warfare" />

The polar opposite of the Empire's mass-, numbers-, and firepower-based tactics were the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Rebel Alliance's]] maneuver-based tactics, which advocated defeating the enemy by incapacitating their decision-making through shock and disruption. Because of the numerical advantage enjoyed by the Empire, [[Alliance Army/Legends|Alliance Army]] commanders were taught to avoid straight-up frontal attacks against the Imperial Army, which could always guarantee victory by bringing in more reinforcements. Instead, Rebel commanders used speed and force concentration to overpower smaller Imperial forces in detail and achieve decisive victory quickly. Furthermore, Rebel commanders were also taught to use psychological warfare to break the enemy's morale prior to battle and encourage in them fear of the Rebel's fierceness and unpredictability, so as to make the enemy more likely to make mistakes such as overreacting to a feint. This form of doctrine encouraged independent thinking in commanders and an emphasis on taking intelligent risks against the enemy.<ref name="The Rebel Alliance Sourcebook">''[[The Rebel Alliance Sourcebook]]''</ref>

Ground battles could vary immensely in size and scale: the [[Battle of Endor/Legends|Battle of Endor]] was intended as an infiltration raid by a small number of troops in support of the space battle in orbit,<ref name="Star Wars: Episode VI Return of the Jedi">{{Film|VI}}</ref> while the [[Battle of Naboo/Legends|Battle of Naboo]] was a series of small engagements to seize control of the [[Theed Royal Palace/Legends|Theed Royal Palace]] while a larger battle was fought on the [[Great Grass Plains/Legends|Great Grass Plains]] as a diversion and a space battle was fought in support.<ref name="Star Wars: Episode I The Phantom Menace">{{Film|I}}</ref> In contrast, the [[First Battle of Geonosis/Legends|First Battle of Geonosis]] involved nearly 200,000 [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Republic]] [[Clone trooper/Legends|clone troopers]] and in excess of a million [[Confederacy of Independent Systems/Legends|Separatist]] [[Battle droid/Legends|battle droids]] and many thousands of vehicles across many miles of ground.<ref name="Star Wars: Episode II Attack of the Clones">{{Film|II}}</ref> In addition, although ground warfare was generally considered a separate form of combat from space warfare and starfighter combat, there have been instances where they had direct interaction. Aside from the noted elements of planetary assault operations, a particularly notable example of combined fronts of space and ground warfare was the Battle of Endor, which featured a combination of both elements.<ref name="Star Wars: Episode VI Return of the Jedi">{{Film|VI}}</ref>

There are some cases where ground warfare was conducted by accident and was not the intended conflict. A particularly notable instance of this is the [[Battle of Hoth/Legends|Battle of Hoth]], where the Imperials intended to launch a bombardment at the Rebel-owned Echo Base at a far enough distance to avoid picking up detection from the Rebel scanners, but the hasty actions of the then-''de jure'' leader of [[Death Squadron/Legends|Death Squadron]], [[Admiral/Legends|Admiral]] [[Kendal Ozzel/Legends|Kendal Ozzel]], resulted in the Rebel forces generating a [[Planetary shield/Legends|planetary shield]] around the base, forcing the Imperial forces to conduct a costly ground campaign to defeat the Rebel forces, and the Rebels buying enough time for most of their forces to escape.<ref name="Star Wars: Episode V The Empire Strikes Back">{{Film|V}}</ref>
